speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned rectal bleeding and a palpable rectal mass; can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if you are experiencing any pain or changes in bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 45-year-old female. The patient reports a 2-week history of rectal bleeding occurring daily with bowel movements. She denies any pain with defecation and does not present with any other complaints.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Rectal Carcinoma. The combination of a palpable rectal mass, daily rectal bleeding for two weeks, and a lack of pain suggests a malignant growth rather than hemorrhoids or fissures. I recommend an urgent colonoscopy with biopsy and a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to stage the disease.
